meta.title: Paper 1 Higher November 2020 Walkthrough
meta.subject: Physics
meta.objective: Walk through a real Paper 1 Higher and mark my answers with the real mark scheme

objectives: Answer every question on a real AQA Paper 1 Higher
Mark my answers against the real AQA mark scheme
Spot where marks are lost and correct my answers in purple pen

questions.q: Write the equation that links elastic potential energy, spring constant and extension.
questions.a: elastic potential energy = 0.5 × spring constant × (extension)², Ee = ½ k e²

questions.q: A house wall has a low thermal conductivity. What does this mean?
questions.a: The rate of energy transfer through the wall by conduction is low

questions.q: Two resistors are connected in series. How do you find their total resistance?
questions.a: Add them: R total = R1 + R2

questions.q: A polythene rod is rubbed with a cloth and becomes negatively charged. Explain why.
questions.a: Electrons are transferred from the cloth to the rod

questions.q: What is meant by the specific latent heat of a substance?
questions.a: The energy needed to change the state of 1 kg of the substance with no change in temperature
A high-speed electron emitted from the nucleus (a neutron turns into a proton)

engage.title: LEARNING OBJECTIVES
engage.hook: Today we go through a real GCSE Physics Paper 1, one question at a time.
engage.content:
1. Answer every question on the AQA Paper 1 Higher (November 2020).
2. Mark my answers against the real AQA mark scheme.
3. Spot where marks are lost and correct my answers in purple pen.

build.modelAnswer: I drew {1}an ammeter as a circle with an A inside it and a voltmeter as a circle with a V inside it.{/1} The {2}voltmeter is connected in parallel with the lamp,{/2} across its two ends, and the {3}ammeter is connected in series with the lamp,{/3} in the main loop of the circuit.
doesNotAward: Examiner report: a common mistake was drawing a line through the circle of the ammeter or the voltmeter

build.modelAnswer: My line is {1}a smooth curve with the same shape as the positive half, bending the opposite way,{/1} and it {2}passes through −4.0 V, −0.2 A and carries on to −6.0 V, −0.23 A.{/2}

indicativeContent.text: smooth curved line of correct shape
passing through - 4.0 V, - 0.2 A **or** – 6.0 V, - 0.23 A

doesNotAward: do not accept a line that becomes horizontal

rows.q: 01.3 Equation linking current, potential difference and resistance
rows.a: potential difference = current × resistance   or   V = IR

build.ecfNote: allow 1.0 = their I × R provided their I has been obtained from the graph; allow R = 1.0 ÷ their I; allow an answer consistent with their I
doesNotAward: Examiner report: a common mistake was misreading the current as 0.8 A rather than 0.08 A

rows.q: 01.5 What is meant by a zero error?
rows.a: The ammeter displays a reading when it is not connected (to a circuit). Not: 'the ammeter read zero all the time'.

rows.q: 02.1 Which diagram shows the correct circuit for the torch?
rows.a: all three cells face the same way and the LED points the way the current flows

rows.q: 02.2 Equation linking charge flow, current and time
rows.a: charge flow = current × time   or   Q = It

build.ecfNote: allow a correct substitution using an incorrectly/not converted value of I; allow a correct calculation using an incorrectly/not converted value of I
doesNotAward: Examiner report: many did not convert 50 mA to amps, or converted it wrongly

build.modelAnswer: The LED is a diode. {1}Charge will not flow through a diode in the reverse direction,{/1} because {2}a diode has a very high resistance in the reverse direction.{/2} So there is no current and the LED does not light.

indicativeContent.text: there is no current in a diode (in the reverse direction) **or** charge will not flow through a diode (in the reverse direction)
allow diode will not conduct (electric charge)
(because) a diode has a (very) high resistance (in the reverse direction)

doesNotAward: do not accept the circuit is not complete
Examiner report: answers about polarity that did not mention the LED (diode) scored zero

rows.q: 02.5 Equation linking efficiency, total power input and useful power output
rows.a: efficiency = useful power output ÷ total power input   (no × 100 needed)

modelAnswer: efficiency = useful power output ÷ total power input
doesNotAward: Examiner report: multiplying the final answer by 100 lost the last mark

rows.q: 03.1 Equation linking density, mass and volume
rows.a: density = mass ÷ volume   or   ρ = m ÷ V

build.ecfNote: allow a correct conversion of their calculated value of mass into standard form
doesNotAward: Examiner report: copying errors, e.g. 988 kg/m³ instead of 998, or adding or losing a 0 in the volume

rows.q: 03.3 Equation linking energy transferred, power and time
rows.a: energy transferred = power × time   or   E = Pt

build.ecfNote: allow a correct substitution using an incorrectly/not converted value of t; allow a correct calculation using an incorrectly/not converted value of t
doesNotAward: Examiner report: converting 5 hours into minutes instead of seconds (a correct calculation in minutes scored 2 marks)

build.modelAnswer: First, {1}the increase in demand, from about 30 × 10⁹ W at 04:00 to about 49 × 10⁹ W at 16:00, is much greater than the 1.5 × 10⁹ W the power station can provide.{/1} Second, {2}demand stays high from 04:00 to 16:00, which is 12 hours, longer than the maximum of 5 hours.{/2}

indicativeContent.text: the variation in demand is (much) greater than 1.5 × 10⁹ W
allow the increase in demand is greater than the (power) output of the (hydroelectric) power station
demand remains high for longer than 5 hours
allow 04:00 to 16:00 is 12 hours; allow 04:00 to 16:00 is greater than 5 hours

doesNotAward: Examiner report: answers about people using more energy in the day, or weather, waves, wind or tides, with no data from the graph
Examiner report: 68% and 312.5% were common answers and both scored 0 marks

build.modelAnswer: A gas-fired power station releases {1}no sulfur dioxide,{/1} so it does not cause acid rain. It also releases {2}less carbon dioxide per kg of fuel burned,{/2} so it adds less to global warming.

indicativeContent.text: less carbon dioxide released (per kg of fuel burned)
less global warming (allow less climate change; allow less greenhouse gases)
gas mining is less destructive than coal mining

doesNotAward: ignore less air pollution
Examiner report: gas is NOT renewable and DOES release carbon dioxide

build.modelAnswer: The data show that {1}the mean sea surface temperature shows a steady increase{/1} {2}from 16.45 °C in 1988 to 16.96 °C in 2016.{/2} The sea is getting warmer over time, which suggests that climate change is happening.

indicativeContent.text: mean sea surface temperature shows a (steady) increase
over the time period on the graph **or** from 16.45 (°C) to 16.96 (°C)
allow between a correct pair of dates at least 10 years apart; allow a correct pair of temperatures at least 10 years apart

doesNotAward: Examiner report: a general upward trend with no time period or data usually scored only 1 mark

build.modelAnswer: I would choose {1}thermistor C,{/1} because {2}its change in resistance is greatest{/2} {3}between 0 and 25 °C,{/3} which is the range of sea surface temperatures. This makes it the most sensitive to a small change in temperature.

indicativeContent.text: (because) the change in resistance is greatest
allow the gradient is highest; allow more sensitive to temperature change
between 0 and 25 ºC (allow between 16 and 17 ºC)

if thermistor C is not chosen, allow for 1 mark each: not thermistor A because there is no/little change in resistance; not thermistor B as there is only a small change in resistance; not thermistor D as there is no data available between 0 and 40 ºC

doesNotAward: Examiner report: most chose thermistor A 'because it has the lowest resistance'

rows.q: 05.1 One other man-made source of background radiation
rows.a: medical x-rays (or radiotherapy, nuclear weapons testing, a named nuclear disaster e.g. Chernobyl / Fukushima). Ignore radioactive / nuclear waste.
uranium or plutonium (allow thorium). Not coal, oil or gas.

build.modelAnswer: {1}A neutron is absorbed by a uranium nucleus.{/1} The nucleus becomes unstable and {2}splits into two parts,{/2} two smaller daughter nuclei, {3}and two or three neutrons are released{/3} {4}and gamma rays are emitted.{/4} Energy is released in the process.

indicativeContent.text: neutron absorbed by a uranium nucleus
nucleus splits into two parts (allow an atom splits into two parts if 1st marking point doesn't score)

doesNotAward: Examiner report: the neutron only 'colliding with' the nucleus, or being absorbed by an 'atom', was not enough

build.modelAnswer: In nuclear fusion, {1}two lighter nuclei join to form a heavier nucleus.{/1} {2}Some of the mass of the nuclei is converted into energy,{/2} which is released as radiation.

indicativeContent.text: lighter nuclei join to form heavier nuclei (allow specific examples)
some of the mass (of the nuclei) is converted to energy (of radiation)

doesNotAward: Examiner report: 'atoms fuse' or 'elements fuse' was not enough; nor were bonds breaking or exothermic reactions

build.modelAnswer: With a shorter half-life, {1}the activity of the waste decreases quickly,{/1} so {2}the risk of harm from the waste decreases quickly.{/2} The burial site would not need to be monitored for as long.

indicativeContent.text: activity decreases quickly (allow nuclei / waste will decay at a greater rate)
allow burial site doesn't need to be monitored for as long **or** doesn't need to be buried underground for as long **or** may not need to be buried underground

doesNotAward: ignore waste is radioactive for less time
Examiner report: vague 'less harm to the environment' was not enough

rows.q: 06.1 Which two measurements are needed to find the speed of a rider and sled?
rows.a: Length of sled and Time for sled to pass light gate (1 mark each)

build.ecfNote: allow a correct substitution / rearrangement / calculation using an incorrectly/not converted value of Ep
doesNotAward: Examiner report: not converting kJ to J gave 0.05 kg; 8330 ÷ 9.8 × 17.0 gave 1445 kg

build.modelAnswer: As each rider slides down, {1}the decrease in Ep equals the increase in Ek, so ½mv² = mgh.{/1} {2}The mass cancels on both sides of the equation, giving v² = 2gh,{/2} so {3}the final speed only depends on the vertical height and the gravitational field strength,{/3} not on the mass. Small differences in speed are {4}due to air resistance and friction, or a different starting speed.{/4}

indicativeContent.text: ½ mv² = mgh **or** decrease in Ep = increase in Ek
masses cancel on both sides of the equation **or** v² = 2gh
(final) speed only depends on vertical height (and gravitational field strength)
variations will be due to air resistance/friction **or** different initial speed

doesNotAward: Examiner report: terminal velocity answers did not score (the slide is not high enough to reach it)

rows.q: 07.1 Why did the temperature not start to increase straight away?
rows.a: The heating element of the kettle takes time to heat up (allow the kettle takes time to heat up). Not: 'water has a high specific heat capacity'.

build.ecfNote: allow a correct substitution / rearrangement / calculation of mass using an incorrect value of Δθ
doesNotAward: Examiner report: using a temperature change of 100 °C gave 0.37 (4 marks)

build.modelAnswer: {1}The gradient of the straight section is the temperature change ÷ time, the rate of temperature increase.{/1} The energy transferred is E = Pt and also E = m × c × temperature change, so {2}Pt = m × c × temperature change.{/2} Dividing both sides by t gives {3}P = gradient × m × c,{/3} using the mass of the water and its specific heat capacity.

indicativeContent.text: Gradient = Δθ ÷ t (allow gradient = rate of temperature increase; allow calculation of gradient)

doesNotAward: Examiner report: using the horizontal section, or the efficiency equation, did not score

build.modelAnswer: {1}Precise results show little variation,{/1} so they are close together. {2}The fourth reading, 16.2 ohms, is further away from the mean than the other values,{/2} so it makes the spread bigger and does not make the results more precise.

indicativeContent.text: the 4th result was further away from the mean than the other values (allow the range of values has increased)

doesNotAward: ignore the 4th result was an anomaly
Examiner report: precision is not the resolution of an instrument; 'it increases the accuracy not the precision' did not score

build.modelAnswer: If n is inversely proportional to R, then n × R is a constant. From Figure 12, {1}2 × 24 = 48 and 3 × 16 = 48,{/1} and {2}4 × 12 = 48.{/2} {3}So n × R = constant (48), showing the student was correct.{/3}

indicativeContent.text: two pairs of values of n and R showing that n × R = constant
third pair of values of n and R showing that n × R = constant
(so) n × R = constant (showing the student was correct)
allow 1 mark each for two statements relating the change in number of resistors to the change in (mean total) resistance; allow 1 mark for use of data from graph to confirm at least one statement

doesNotAward: Examiner report: 'as one goes up the other goes down' scored no marks

build.modelAnswer: Adding a resistor in parallel gives {1}another path for the charge to flow through,{/1} so for the same potential difference {2}the total current is greater.{/2} A greater total current for the same potential difference means a smaller total resistance.

indicativeContent.text: multiple paths for charge / electrons to flow (allow current for charge)
total current is greater (for the same potential difference when more resistors are added)

doesNotAward: Examiner report: 'the resistance is shared' was the most common answer and scored nothing

indicativeContent.text: alternative approach for 4th and 5th marks: 5.75 = 0.025² × R (1) or R = 5.75 ÷ 0.025², R = 9200 (Ω) (1); alternative approach: 5.75 = 230² ÷ R (3), R = 230² ÷ 5.75 (1), R = 9200 (Ω) (1)

build.ecfNote: allow a correct substitution / rearrangement / calculation of resistance using an incorrect value of I
doesNotAward: Examiner report: P = IV rearranged wrongly to I = V ÷ P

build.modelAnswer: The switch is on the live side, so {1}one wire in the switch is live,{/1} at a potential of 230 V. {2}The electrician is earthed, at earth potential.{/2} So {3}there would be a large potential difference between the live wire and the electrician,{/3} and a current would flow through him if he touched the wire.

indicativeContent.text: one wire in the switch is live (allow the switch / circuit is live; allow one wire is at a potential of 230 V)
the electrician is earthed **or** the electrician is at earth potential
(so) there will be a (large) potential difference between the live wire and the electrician / earth (if the electrician touched the wire)

doesNotAward: Examiner report: 'potential difference of the live wire' instead of its potential lost the third mark

build.modelAnswer: From Figure 14, {1}50 Hz has the lowest maximum let-go current, about 9 mA.{/1} {2}At a different frequency, such as 100 Hz, people could let go at a greater current, about 16 mA,{/2} so they are less likely to be stuck holding the circuit.

indicativeContent.text: 50 Hz has the lowest (maximum) let-go current
a higher / lower / different frequency would allow people to let go at a greater current (allow a specific numerical example as opposed to a trend)

doesNotAward: Examiner report: just reading values off the graph, with no explanation of what they mean, was not enough

rows.q: 10.1 Which statements describe the movement of the gas particles?
rows.a: The particles move in random directions. The particles move with a range of speeds. (1 mark each)

build.ecfNote: allow correct substitution into p1V1 = p2V2 for first 2 marking points; allow a correct substitution / rearrangement / calculation using an incorrect value of the constant
doesNotAward: Examiner report: pressure ÷ volume = constant is wrong

build.modelAnswer: When the temperature increases, {1}the particles have a higher mean kinetic energy,{/1} so they move faster. This means {2}there is an increased number of collisions with the walls of the balloon per second,{/2} and {3}greater forces are exerted in the collisions with the balloon walls.{/3} {4}A greater force is exerted on the same area,{/4} so the pressure increases.

indicativeContent.text: particles would have a higher (mean) kinetic energy (allow particles would have a higher (mean) speed)
(so) increased number of collisions with the walls of the balloon per second (allow greater frequency of collisions with the walls of the balloon)
greater forces exerted in collisions (between particles and balloon walls) (allow greater rate of change of momentum (of particles))
greater force exerted on same area (allow description using p = F/A)

doesNotAward: do not accept particles vibrate more
Examiner report: pressure is NOT caused by particles colliding with each other
